Handsome, shallow, and ultra-muscular, Jim Queen is a gay influencer content to live off his looks. Thin, insecure, and closeted, Lucien is one of Jim’s many followers. When the gym-bod god gets infected with Heterosis — a drug manufactured by the far-right that causes heterosexuality — the two men must join forces and find a cure for straightness before Jim’s online clout runs out.

Brought to life by directors Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané, JIM QUEEN is a perfect satirical creation: Jim’s vanity and superficiality make for a great sendup of gay “body fascism”. Of course, the filmmakers reserve much of their scorn for homophobic conservatism, and the inversion of homo- and heterosexuality is provocative and hilarious. From the opening musical number to the spoof of conversion therapy to an outrageous Trojan-horse gag and beyond, JIM QUEEN is a raucous delight.

Audience Award, VIFF 2026

JIM QUEEN (Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané, 2026 / 2026 / 85 mins / 14A / French w.EST) A gay influencer’s life crumbles when a virus turns gay men in Paris straight. He teams up with a twink to search for a rumored cure in the Marais in this satire on fame and culture.

An incisive look behind the legend of Elon Musk, the world’s most heralded “inventor-entrepreneur” who has enormous influence on the world in which we all live.

MUSK (Alex Gibney, 2026 / PG / 235 mins) A thorough and unvarnished analysis of Elon Musk, a technology billionaire who serves as the CEO of Tesla, SpaceX, and Twitter.

In TRACES OF HOME, filmmaker Colette Ghunim embarks on journeys with her parents to find the ancestral houses they were forced to flee as children in Mexico and Palestine. What begins as a desire to connect to Colette’s cultural origins reveals an internal quest to heal her disconnect with her parents, and, ultimately, with herself.

Filmmakers including Executive Producer Dr. Gabor Maté and director Colette Ghunim wil be joining us for a post-show talk-back following the screening.

“In ‘Traces of Home’, our past has a way of resurfacing no matter how hard we try to bury it. Only by confronting those old wounds can we find a new path to walk together.” (Film Threat)

Shot entirely in Nanaimo, BC, local filmmaker Sam Adolph brings his newest feature, FIGHT! FIGHT! FIGHT! to the Rio Theatre for an exclusive Vancouver premiere for one night only!

Matthew Bowman is a lonely call center employee living an apathetic and confusing life. At work, his days consist of attempted cold call sales which are often met with rejection and a boss who’s superiority complex is unmatched. At home he finds himself lost in the infinite sea of ad campaigns on TV, featuring controversial politician: Jimmy Joblinski.

The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers.

Feeling a spur of uncharacteristic spontaneity, Matthew accepts an invitation to a local punk show. At this show he meets another young man, Jacob Mauser. Matthew sees in Jacob what he lacks in himself, confidence, charisma, and a sense of purpose.

As the election looms, Matthew’s eyes are opened to Jacob and his friends’ vastly different worldview. One of sex, drugs and protest.

After an evening of lsd infused partying, Matthew Bowman wakes up in his car on the side of a dirt road… And discovers something that will forever change the course of his life, forcing him to reckon with the nightmare that his life has unraveled into, along with the battlefield his mind has become.

“First of all, keep him out of the light, he hates bright light, especially sunlight, it’ll kill him. Second, don’t give him any water, not even to drink. But the most important rule, the rule you can never forget, no matter how much he cries, no matter how much he begs, never feed him after midnight…”

Join us at the Rio Theatre for a very special screening of Joe Dante’s classic 1984 horror-comedy GREMLINS, followed by a conversation with its star, actor Zach Galligan. Zach (who played Billy Peltzer in both the original film and its 1990 sequel, GREMLINS 2: THE NEW BATCH) will be on-hand following the film to chat about the iconic franchise, share memories and stories, and take your questions. The evening’s festivities will be hosted and moderated by Tanner Zipchen.

Even better? Following the Q&A, every ticket-holder will have a chance to get a Christmas photo with Zach and Gizmo – so deck the halls and dust off your favourite seasonally-appropriate sweater!

When a gadget salesman is looking for that special Christmas gift for his son Billy, he happens upon something totally unusual at an old store in Chinatown. Though the shopkeeper is reluctant to sell him the adorable “Mogwai,” creature, he sells it to him anyway –  with a few important caveats. Never expose him to bright light, water, or to feed him after midnight. When the instructions aren’t followed, chaos ensues when a gang of mischevious, lizard-like gremlins appear, wreaking havoc and tearing up the Norman Rockwell-esque  town on Christmas Eve. Starring Phoebe Cates, Zach Galligan, Corey Feldman, Polly Holliday, Keye Luke and… Gizmo.

The COAST MOUNTAIN FILM FEST turns the Rio Theatre over to snowboarders for a late-night throwback to one of the most memorable team films of its era.

CAPiTA: DEFENDERS OF AWESOME hit screens in 2011 with a stacked roster of riders and quickly became a snapshot of an incredible period in snowboard culture. Featuring some of the biggest names in the sport — including nominees for ‘Men’s Rider of the Year,’ ‘Women’s Rider of the Year’ and ‘Rookie of the Year’ — it delivers huge riding, unmistakable style and the energy of classic snowboard filmmaking.

Now CAPiTA: DEFENDERS OF AWESOME is coming back to the big screen for a proper throwback celebration.

Grab your crew and join a theatre full of snowboarders for films, prizes, good times and a healthy dose of nostalgia as we get ready for another winter in the mountains. And, sure, we’ll show some amazing shorts from the 2026 season too!

From early-season preparation and road trips to storm cycles, team hangs and unforgettable days in the mountains, the film mixes incredible ski action with a behind-the-scenes look at everything that goes into a season on the move.

The night also features THE WAY OF SNOW | Yuki no Michi, a short film from Japan featuring two Whistler athletes and a distinctly different perspective on life in the mountains.
Come get frothy with a theatre full of skiers, celebrate the start of winter and enjoy a night of films, prizes and mountain culture on the big screen.

THE PROPHET OF ECSTASY explores themes of art, politics and consciousness through the improbable life of Michael Clegg, the former Catholic priest who introduced MDMA to the world – a drug he would later dub ‘Ecstasy’. The documentary will take viewers on a wild ride, from Clegg’s life as an MDMA drug kingpin, to his present-day transformation as an enlightened yogi. It also examines how the destinies of Michael Clegg, chemist Carina Leveriza, and psychedelics advocate Rick Doblin, are inexorably bound with that of the socio-cultural explosion of MDMA through its epic journey of discovery, criminalization, and re-emergence from the shadows.

Official selection of the The Psychedelic Film and Music Festival in New York – 2026.

Official selection, The Psychedelic Film and Music Festival in New York 2026, Catalina Film Festival 2026

Presented by Laurus Productions and MAPS Canada
Sponsored by QI Integrated Health &  Gathering Groups
Community Partners: Psygen, Roots To Thrive, TheraPsil, Psychedelic Association of Canada

Moderated by Lori Braun (Producer), with psychedelic advocate Rick Doblin, PhD, mycologist Paul Stamets, psychedelic-medicine researcher Dr. Pamela Kryskow, and veteran psychedelic chemist Peter van der Heyden, PhD.

Doors 5:00 pm l Movie 5:30 pm *Start times subject to change. Please arrive on time

Panel Discussion:

Following the screening of Prophet of Ecstasy, stay for a provocative conversation with the filmmakers as well as – Rick Doblin, PhD, psychedelic pioneer and founder of MAPS, Paul Stamets, world-renowned mycologist, Dr. Pamela Kryskow, psychedelic-medicine researcher, and medical lead at Roots to Thrive and Peter van der Heyden, PhD, veteran psychedelic chemist and co-founder of Psygen.

From shifting drug laws and the fight for psychedelic access to the wild true story behind the film, the panel dives into where the psychedelic movement is now, what still needs to change, and what comes next.

“This documentary opened up my mind better than any drug would, as it told me a lot of interesting facts and crazy things that happened through this whole drug craze.” (Hollywood North Magazine)

“Prophet of Ecstasy is an interesting story about the rise and fall of a psychedelic drug empire.” (Sean Kelly on Movies)

“The film impressively shows how a stigmatized substance evolved from a socio-cultural explosion in the underground to a beacon of hope in modern psychotherapy. “ (Psychedelia-Stiftung)

“He’s a figure in the psychedelics movement who established ecstasy as a go-to party drug with therapeutic potential — and a lasting impact on the culture. “(CBC DOCS)

THE PROPHET OF ECSTASY (Karen Cho, Elias Varoutsos, 2026 / 101 mins / G) explores themes of art, politics and consciousness through the improbable life of Michael Clegg, the former Catholic seminarian who introduced MDMA to the world – a drug he would later dub ‘Ecstasy’. The documentary will take viewers on a wild ride, from Clegg’s life as an MDMA drug kingpin, to his present-day transformation as an enlightened yogi. It also examines how the destinies of Michael Clegg, chemist Carina Leveriza, and psychedelics advocate Rick Doblin, are inexorably bound with that of the socio-cultural explosion of MDMA through its epic journey of discovery, criminalization, and re-emergence from the shadows.

Composer Claudio Simonetti has written and recorded some of the most influential scores and soundtracks in horror, including SUSPIRIA, DAWN OF THE DEAD, DEEP RED / PROFONDO ROSSO, DEMONS and many others, with his seminal work still informing the genre to this day.
This year, Simonetti’s Goblin returns to the Rio Theatre to celebrate Dario Argento‘s critically-acclaimed 1982 classic, TENEBRE, with a live performance of the score set to a screening of the film. Following the finale of the movie, the collective will return after a brief intermission to deliver an additional performance of quintessential Goblin material and “best of” songs and scores set to their cinematic counterparts.

The Rio Theatre‘s deep dive into Halloween classics continues on October 26 with a 30th Anniversary screening Wes Craven‘s game-changing 1996 slasher comedy (yes, that’s a thing) SCREAM.

“Horror icon Wes Craven’s subversive deconstruction of the genre is sly, witty, and surprisingly effective as a slasher film itself, even if it’s a little too cheeky for some.” (Rotten Tomatoes)

“No one will ever consider Wes Craven’s ‘Scream’ as Oscar fodder, but this funny and scary little experiment in terror from the man who invented “Nightmare on Elm Street” puts some fun back into a very tired genre.” (Newsweek)

SCREAM (Wes Craven 1996 /  111 min / 14A) The sleepy little town of Woodsboro just woke up screaming. There’s a killer in their midst who’s seen a few too many scary movies. Suddenly nobody is safe, as the psychopath stalks victims, taunts them with trivia questions, then rips them to bloody shreds. It could be anybody…

“They’re all gonna laugh at you!”

The Rio Theatre’s annual deep-dive into Halloween movie goodness continues on Sunday, October 25 with a 50th Anniversary screening of Brian de Palma‘s CARRIE.

In this chilling adaptation of Stephen King‘s horror novel, withdrawn and sensitive teen Carrie White (Sissy Spacek) faces taunting from classmates at school and abuse from her fanatically pious mother (Piper Laurie) at home. When strange occurrences start happening around Carrie, she begins to suspect that she has supernatural powers. Invited to the prom by the empathetic Tommy Ross (William Katt), Carrie tries to let her guard down, but things eventually take a dark and violent turn. With John Travolta, Amy Irving, Betty Buckley.

As always, audience costumes (including ghoulish 70s prom attire!) are very welcome – and encouraged!

CARRIE (Brian De Palma, 1976 / 98 mins / 18A) Carrie White, a shy, friendless teenage girl who is sheltered by her domineering, religious mother, unleashes her telekinetic powers after being humiliated by her classmates at her senior prom.

Whether you’re a Virgin or a veteran, you’ll have a blast!

As always, costumes and audience participation are highly encouraged – because costume contest! (In other words: Prizes! Here’s your chance to go all out and let your freak flag fly, people.) The ticket price includes a fun prop bag, too!

Your own props are also very welcome, but please – whatever you do – DO NOT BRING RICE OR CONFETTI!

THE ROCKY HORROR PICTURE SHOW (Jim Sharman, 1975 / 100 mins / 14A) A newly engaged couple (Susan Sarandon, Barry Bostwick) have a breakdown in an isolated area and must pay a call to the bizarre residence of Dr. Frank-N-Furter (Tim Curry), a transvestite scientist. As their innocence is lost, Brad and Janet meet a houseful of wild characters, including a rocking biker and a creepy butler. Through elaborate dances and rock songs, Frank-N-Furter unveils his latest creation: a muscular man named ‘Rocky’.

Now is the time.
This is the hour.
Ours is the magic.
Ours is the power.

Unleash your inner-90’s witchy-self and get into the Halloween spirit with a 30th Anniversary, prime time screening of THE CRAFT.

Neve Campbell, Fairuza Balk, Robin Tunney and Rachel True star as a group of misfit girls on the fringe of their high school crowd who band together to form a unique clique (or, perhaps, “coven”) of their own. What starts out as just harmless fun – getting back at those people who’d slight them – soon grows out of control. Also starring Skeet Ulrich, Christine Taylor, and Breckin Meyer.

“The great strength of ‘The Craft’ is that it doesn’t pass judgment on why the girls are doing what they do… The film’s message of female empowerment felt cathartic, but so did its rage.” (Refinery29)

THE CRAFT (Andrew Fleming, 1996 / 111 mins) When newcomer Sarah moves to a new city with her family to start a new life, she makes fast friends with some of the girls in her schoool who are just as “on the fringe” as she is. A shared interest in the occult goes further than they expected as they each attain unusual powers. What starts out as good fun soon turns dangerous.
